content: The Kentucky School for the Deaf was established through the efforts of General Elias Barbee, who had a daughter named Lucy who was deaf. General Barbee proposed a bill to the Kentucky Assembly, which led to the school's placement in Danville under the administration of the Centre College Board of Trustees. In 1825, John Adamson Jacobs assumed the role of principal of the school. Since its founding, the institution has been overseen by 14 superintendents, with its current leadership under Dr. Harvey Jay Corson. One of the campus's most historically significant structures, Jacobs Hall, is recognized as a National Historic Landmark. The school's athletic teams are known by the nickname Colonels. While their athletic achievements have been modest overall, they have managed to secure at least one championship in high school 8-man football.
